name: Starter: Malay
about: Malay in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Malay order.

words.mana: which; di mana: where; ke mana: where to

words.masak: cook (memasak: to cook; masakan: cooking, dishes)

gembira-berjumpa.about: Literally glad meet with you; dengan anda to someone you'd call anda.

terima-kasih.about: Literally receive love; terima kasih banyak-banyak: thanks a lot.

concept.line: Many action verbs are built from a root with a beginning that changes with the root's first sound: masak → memasak (cook), baca → membaca (read), cuci → mencuci (wash).

words.means: please (before a request for action); help

concept.line: Before a describing word, Malay needs no is: Saya lapar (I hungry), Rumah itu besar (house that big); ialah links two nouns in careful speech, never a describing word.
The owner comes after the thing, and saya (I, me) also means my: rumah saya (house my), kereta ayah saya (car father my: my father's car).
di is at or in, ke is to and dari is from: di rumah (at home), ke pasar (to market), dari pejabat (from office).
A question word can sit where its answer would go, as in Awak tinggal di mana?
ada says there is or there are, and after someone, they have: Ada roti (exist bread), Saya ada kereta (I have car); tidak ada is there isn't.
